question: My CRA account's displayed TFSA contribution room does not yet reflect a recent withdrawal. Which records should I use to avoid making an excess contribution?
generated_answer:
To avoid making an excess contribution, use the most recent records from the CRA's My CRA account. If the account does not yet reflect a recent withdrawal, you can use the following steps:

1. Check your CRA account regularly for updates on your TFSA contribution room.
2. If the withdrawal is not reflected, use the most recent available information from the CRA.
3. If you have any doubts or discrepancies, contact the CRA directly for clarification on your current contribution room.

Remember, it's always better to err on the side of caution and use the most conservative estimate to avoid over-contributing to your TFSA. If you have already made a withdrawal, you can also use the following formula to calculate your available contribution room:

Available contribution room = (Total TFSA contribution room) - (Withdrawals made in the current year)

If you're still unsure, consider waiting until the CRA updates your account to reflect the recent withdrawal before making any new contributions. This will help ensure you stay within your allowed limits and avoid any potential penalties. 

For more information, you can refer to the CRA's official guide on TFSA contribution limits and rules: [https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/tax-free-savings-account/contribution-limits.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/tax-free-savings-account/contribution-limits.html) 

If you have any further questions or concerns, I recommend reaching out to the CRA directly for personalized assistance.
